subtitle: Journal-club style ICU update: PICO, key results, appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English.

script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for November 07, 2026.
Today we will review 3 recent ICU-relevant publications.

Use this as a morning triage tool, then open the source link for full-text appraisal before changing practice.

articles.title: Impact of the updated SOFA-2 score on organ dysfunction assessment and trial outcomes in Sepsis: A reanalysis of two randomized trials.
articles.summary: For the ACTS primary outcome, SOFA-2 (mean difference [MD] -0.8, 95% CI -1.6 to 0.0, p = 0.06) was similar to SOFA-1 (MD -0.8, 95% CI -1.7 to 0.2, p = 0.12) but became significant in the post hoc, exploratory urine-output analysis (MD -0.84, 95% CI -1.64 to -0.05, p = 0.04). The Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score is the standard tool for quantifying organ dysfunction in sepsis. The updated SOFA-2 score may alter interpretation of prior trials. We reanalyzed two adult sepsis randomized trials, Ascorbic Acid, Corticosteroids, and Thiamine in Sepsis (ACTS) and Thiamine for Renal Protection in Septic Shock (TRPSS), to evaluate the impact of SOFA-2 on organ-specific scoring and trial interpretation. Patient data were rescored using a best available SOFA-2 reconstruction.

articles.title: Vasoactive-Adjusted Shock Index for Risk Stratification in Adult Sepsis.
articles.summary: A total of 63853 patients was included. The high VASI group had markedly higher 28-day mortality (HR 2.89, 95% CI 2.72-3.08) and 90-day mortality (HR 2.85, 95% CI 2.68-3.03). Albumin showed a protective effect only in the low VASI group (OR 0.667, 95% CI 0.545-0.816), but the interaction was not significant. However, no significant heterogeneity of treatment effect was observed for hydrocortisone or albumin in different VASI trajectories. The vasoactive-adjusted shock index (VASI) has been shown to identify a refractory shock phenotype in pediatric sepsis that is associated with high mortality.
